messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER: oncall (priya.k) - High severity: multiple inference nodes in us-west-2-infer are transitioning to NotReady. Potential customer impact on low-latency routes. See /incidents/INC-2030 for details.
Priya K.: Seeing alerts - cpu pressure + kubelet restart flaps on 3 nodes. Metrics show GPU driver restarts and `OOM` for a couple of runtime containers. Pulling logs now.
Priya K.: @Maya can you check if any recent infra changes in us-west-2? config/daemonset updates?
Maya (platform): no infra deploys in the region in the last 6 hours. No recent GPU driver rollouts. CI image deploy finished earlier but not targeted to infer nodes.
Dan R.: I'm jumping in. Priya, what's the cluster autoscaler doing? Are pods stuck Pending?
Priya K.: Autoscaler attempted scale-up but several pods evicted with OOMKilled and some failing liveness probes. Kubelet restarted on node-uw2-infer-07 at 2030123570.
Ash C.: Copy. Pinging cloud team to check node-level events and potential kernel OOMs.
Priya K.: Paste of a quick `kubectl -n inference describe node node-uw2-infer-07` snippet:
```
Conditions:
  Ready    Unknown  2m (x3 over 10m) kubelet has not reported status
Events:
  Warning  KubeletRestarted  kubelet restarted (reason: Killed process due to OOM)
  Warning  EvictionThresholdMet  memory available below eviction threshold
```
Dan R.: kubelet logs show repeated `SIGSEGV` in nvidia-driver-proxy and `Failed to allocate 0x...` CUDA errors. Likely GPU driver/firmware instability + memory pressure.
Priya K.: Customer-facing routes using the gpu-heavy model (redwood/gpt-llama-13b-q8) are impacted - percent of requests returning 503 has spiked to ~18% in last 10m.
SRE Lead - Jordan: Immediate priorities: 1) stop customer-facing traffic to affected nodes via routing policy 2) reduce memory pressure on nodes (drain/cordon worst offenders) 3) spin up warm standby nodes with the compatible model variant 4) collect full crashlogs for RCA.
Priya K.: I'm starting routing cutover to fallback model pool (cpu-backed smaller model) for low-latency routes to protect user traffic. Will apply canary routing to reduce error rate with minimal quality regression.
deploy-bot: Started route update: scale down fraction=0.7 on route "inference-lowlatency-usw2-gpu" -> fallback-route applied.
Dan R.: Running: `kubectl cordon node-uw2-infer-07 && kubectl drain node-uw2-infer-07 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --force`
Ash C.: Cloud console shows host-level OOM events around same time. Kernel dmesg snapshot attached to incident. Looks like one driver process triggered memory leak after ~3 hours of sustained traffic.
Priya K.: Draining nodes triggered immediate pod restarts and traffic rebalancing. Error rate dropped from 18% -> 6% in ~90s. Latency small bump +10-20ms.
Maya (platform): I'm provisioning two extra nodepools with newer nvidia-driver (staged) and a slightly newer kernel that fixed a known memory regression in the driver release notes. Provision ETA ~7 minutes.
Dan R.: In parallel, I'll patch the inference runtime to enable smaller max-sequence memory caps for models on risky nodes (reduce kv cache growth). Pushing config as transient feature flag.
Priya K.: Collecting pod logs for crashlooping containers: attaching last 200 lines from `inference-runtime` container on one affected pod:
```
2023-... Runtime ERROR: failed to allocate CUDA buffer: out of memory
2023-... Runtime INFO: OOM kill received, attempting graceful shutdown
2023-... Container terminated with exit code 137
```
SRE Lead - Jordan: Good. After we stabilize, we need a follow-up plan: driver rollback/upgrade across region, targeted canary of new nodes, and an eval of batching parameters that may have allowed runaway memory growth.
Priya K.: Quick customer impact note: support page shows increased latency and 5-10% transient errors for customers pinned to the gpu route; we've opened a high-priority incident page and notified Success.
Ash C.: Cloud team reports one hypervisor maintenance + degraded host health for two physical hosts hosting the nodes; moving workloads off host h-uw2-22. Could be correlated with GPU driver resets.
Maya (platform): New nodepool is ready. I've labeled nodes `infer-canary-v2`. Starting canary attach of the model variant (quantized profile) and will monitor memory curves.
deploy-bot: Canary rollout started for model variant redwood/gpt-llama-13b-q8-quant-v2 on nodes labeled infer-canary-v2.
Dan R.: Canary looks stable for 4 minutes - no kernel OOMs, no driver restarts. I'm slowly increasing traffic to canary at 10% intervals.
Priya K.: Error rate back to baseline ~1.2% after full cutover to fallback routes + canary nodes handling most requests. Marking incident mitigation stage: traffic stabilized.
SRE Lead - Jordan: We're keeping cordoned nodes offline for now. Action items: snapshot kernels + driver stacks, collect full heap traces from runtime team, schedule maintenance window for driver upgrade + node replacement tomorrow 06:00 UTC.
Priya K.: I'll own post-incident doc and summarize customer impact + timeline. Dan, assign runtime team ticket to investigate memory growth (link: TKT-2030).
Dan R.: Created TKT-2030: "inference runtime CUDA buffer leak investigation" and assigned to Ash + runtime.
Ash C.: Noted. I'll grab coredumps and check for any interaction between batching heuristics and kv cache growth.
Priya K.: Quick notes for handoff to next oncall (in ~45m): keep canary up, do not uncordon old nodes until cloud confirms host health + driver patch applied. If new NotReady events spike >3 nodes in 10m, escalate to SRE Lead immediately.
SRE Lead - Jordan: Thanks. Priya, Dan — good work. Marking incident status: mitigated, monitoring. Postmortem to follow. :thumbsup:
Priya K.: Thanks team. I'll update the incident page and ping success + customers affected with summary.
Dan R.: Leaving the channel, will be reachable in case of re-escalation.
Maya (platform): I'll keep monitoring node health and will start the maintenance tomorrow.
incident-bot: Incident INC-2030 status updated -> mitigated.
